title: Timed loop invariant for candidate rounds
statement: Let $M$ be a finite Boolean Turing machine, let $x$ be a Boolean input, and let $\mathrm{cfg}$ assign a configuration of $M$ on $x$ to each natural-number rank. Let $\mathrm{accept}$ be a Boolean-valued function on ranks, and let $B,i,\mathrm{count}$ be natural numbers. Suppose the configuration at rank $i+\mathrm{count}$ is halted with output the one-symbol word $[\mathrm{false}]$. Suppose also that for every $j$ with $i\le j<i+\mathrm{count}$ there is a time $t\le B$ such that, if $\mathrm{accept}(j)$ is true, the machine from $\mathrm{cfg}(j)$ is halted after $t$ steps with output $[\mathrm{true}]$, and otherwise it reaches $\mathrm{cfg}(j+1)$ after $t$ steps. Then there is a time $t\le \mathrm{count}\,B$ at which the machine from $\mathrm{cfg}(i)$ is halted with output the one-symbol word containing the Boolean that is true exactly when at least one of the $\mathrm{count}$ ranks starting at $i$ is accepted.
hypotheses_covered: A rank-indexed family of configurations of $M$ on $x$
The endpoint configuration is halted with output $[\mathrm{false}]$
Each rank in the specified interval satisfies the bounded accept-or-advance condition
replaced:
Let $M$ be a finite multi-tape Turing machine over the binary alphabet, $x$ an
input, and let $\mathrm{cfg}$ assign to each rank a configuration of $M$ on $x$.
Suppose the configuration at rank $i + \mathrm{count}$ is halted with single-bit
output false, and that for each rank $j$ with $i \le j < i + \mathrm{count}$ the
machine, within $B$ steps from $\mathrm{cfg}(j)$, either halts with single-bit
output true (when rank $j$ accepts) or reaches $\mathrm{cfg}(j+1)$ (when it
rejects). Then within $\mathrm{count} \cdot B$ steps from $\mathrm{cfg}(i)$ the
machine halts with single-bit output equal to the disjunction of the acceptance
bits over the ranks $i \le j < i + \mathrm{count}$.
